idea: Custom printed T-shirts and hoodies for college fests and clubs

strategist.problem: Club heads and fest committees face a 2-week deadline before their event to source 50-200 custom printed garments, but local print shops charge premium rates for small batches and often miss delivery dates, forcing them to scramble for last-minute, low-quality alternatives or cancel merchandise entirely.
strategist.target_customer: Student club heads and fest committee members at Indian universities with 50-200 member bases who are actively planning events 3-4 weeks out and need to bulk order branded merchandise within a fixed budget.
strategist.mission: Deliver high-quality, custom-printed T-shirts and hoodies to college clubs and fests in 7 days with transparent bulk pricing and 50% advance payment security.

competitors.name: Local college-area print shops
competitors.differentiator: We offer 7-day guaranteed delivery and digital design approval via WhatsApp, whereas local shops have 10-14 day lead times and no digital preview process.

competitors.name: Printrove and similar online print-on-demand platforms
competitors.differentiator: We provide dedicated human support for design iterations and bulk discounts for 50+ units, whereas online platforms have automated, limited support and higher per-unit costs for small batches.

competitors.name: Freelance designers on Fiverr/Upwork
competitors.differentiator: We handle the entire process from design to physical delivery, whereas freelancers only provide digital files, leaving the customer to find a separate printer and manage logistics.

scope_cuts: No custom software or app for order management; we use WhatsApp and Google Sheets to track orders, designs, and payments to save development time and cost.
No in-house printing or equipment purchase; we partner with 2-3 existing local print shops on a per-order basis to avoid capital expenditure and inventory risk.
No retail or single-unit sales; we focus exclusively on bulk orders of 25+ units to maintain margins and simplify logistics for a solo founder.

stack.name: WhatsApp Business
stack.why: Order intake, design approvals and delivery updates with club heads happen in WhatsApp groups and DMs already; catalogue and quick replies replace a custom app.

stack.name: Google Sheets
stack.why: Track every order, size breakdown, design version and 50% advance status in one shared sheet with the part-time helper; no order-management software to build.

stack.name: Razorpay Payment Links
stack.why: Collect the 50% advance and final balance via UPI from fest treasurers; 2% + GST only when a customer pays, no setup fee.

stack.name: Google Sites
stack.why: Free one-page storefront with bulk price list, size chart and sample photos; enough to send a link to a fest committee.

stack.name: Instagram Business account
stack.why: Club heads judge print quality visually; posts and DMs of past bulk orders feed directly into WhatsApp quotes.

stack.name: Google Workspace
stack.why: Free Gmail + Drive + Sheets on a Google account holds quotes, artwork files and the order tracker.

ai_tools.name: Claude
ai_tools.why: Writes quote messages, size-chart copy, follow-up scripts and the supplier negotiation email; Claude Code drafts the Google Sites HTML and Canva-sized asset copy.

ai_tools.name: ChatGPT
ai_tools.why: Generates and iterates club/fest logo mockup concepts and print-ready artwork descriptions to send to the print partner before sampling.

ai_tools.name: Canva
ai_tools.why: Free tier designs the T-shirt front/back mockups, WhatsApp catalogue images and the one-page price poster.

ai_tools.name: Gemini
ai_tools.why: Free Google AI Plus (Indian students: free for a year, redeem by 31 Dec 2026) helps with Sheets formulas for order and margin tracking.

mvp_features: SKU 1: Club Tee — 180 GSM 100% cotton round-neck, 1-colour front logo + 1-colour back text, sizes S-XXL, minimum 25 units, bulk tier pricing on the Google Sites price list.
SKU 2: Fest Tee — 180 GSM cotton, 2-colour front graphic + full-back event name print, sizes S-XXL, minimum 50 units, includes 1 free design revision via WhatsApp.
SKU 3: Hoodie Bundle — 320 GSM fleece-lined pullover hoodie, 1-colour chest logo + back print, sizes S-XXL, minimum 25 units, ordered only after the first tee order is confirmed.

tool_costs.price_note: 2% + GST per payment, no setup fee or AMC. Price checked 2026-11-02 on https://razorpay.com/pricing/

first_10_steps: List 3 college-area print shops within 5 km and WhatsApp each asking for per-unit rates at 25, 50 and 100 units for 180 GSM tee and 320 GSM hoodie, plus exact lead time.
Order 2 sample T-shirts (1 club-style, 1 fest-style) from the cheapest responsive shop, paying under ₹1,200 total, to check print and fabric quality in hand.
Open a free Google Sheet with columns for order ID, club name, event date, SKU, size breakdown, unit price, 50% advance received, balance due, print partner, delivery date.
Build the one-page Google Sites storefront with the bulk price list, size chart, 7-day delivery promise and 3 sample photos; buy the ₹75/mo .in domain.
Create the free WhatsApp Business catalogue with the 3 SKUs and set quick replies for the quote request, size chart and 50% advance payment message.
Generate the logo mockups in ChatGPT and lay them out in Canva free; export 3 mockup images for the Instagram grid and WhatsApp catalogue.
Post the first 3 Instagram posts and send the Google Sites link plus a sample photo to 10 club heads and fest committee members you already know, asking for a 25-unit quote request.
Send a Razorpay payment link for 50% advance on the first confirmed order and record it in the Google Sheet the same day.
Confirm the print slot with the chosen print partner by WhatsApp for the first order's delivery date, sharing the approved artwork file from Google Drive.
Deliver the first bulk order, take 5 photos of the shirts on students, post them on Instagram and ask that club head for one referral to another club.

pricing.name: Hoodie Bundle (25+ units)
features: Ordered after first tee order confirmed

revenue_targets.notes: One-time project revenue: first 50-unit Fest Tee order from a club head already contacted; 50% advance collected via Razorpay; this is a per-order project payment, not recurring MRR
One-time project revenue: second bulk order from a referral by the first club head; hoodie upsell starts; each order is a separate project payment

One-time project revenue: one order per month from fest committee + club; reorder assumption — same club reorders next fest cycle (~1 per quarter), so ~1 of the 3 Day-90 orders is a repeat rather than a new customer

key_assumptions: One bulk order = 50 units x ₹349 avg unit price = ₹17,450 order value; a typical paying customer (one club/fest) pays ₹10,875 in a typical month across tiers — but these are one-time project payments per order, not recurring MRR; reorder assumption: each club/fest reorders once per fest cycle (~1 per quarter)
Delivery cost per customer = goods COGS (~60% of order value ≈ ₹6,500) + print partner coordination + 2 helper hours (₹400) + packaging/shipping (₹1,000) = ₹7,900 per order served
Willingness to pay: fest treasurers already budget ₹300-₹400 per tee for 50+ units from local shops; ₹329-₹349 undercuts them while guaranteeing 7-day delivery
Only 1 order per month is realistic for a student founder at 15 hrs/week during term; break-even is 2 orders because fixed burn is ₹3,575 and per-order margin is ₹2,975 after COGS and fees

channels.name: WhatsApp club & fest committee outreach (campus-first, zero spend)
channels.tactic: Pre-week-1: land 1 warm pilot order from a batchmate-run club or your own class fest at cost (₹349/unit Club Tee, 25 units) with 1 free design revision, to generate the first real delivery photo + 2-line WhatsApp testimonial before any cold outreach. Then join 15 college fest/club WhatsApp groups (tech fest, cultural fest, literary club, robotics, sports meet) via batchmates and seniors; post 1 message per group per week. DM 10 club heads/fest convenors per day on WhatsApp + Instagram with the 3-line cold message and a Canva mockup of THEIR club logo on a tee, attaching the pilot delivery photo as proof. Follow up day 3 and day 7. Target: 70 DMs/week, 15 conversations/week.

channels.name: Instagram DM + boosted reel proof (club merch showcase)
channels.tactic: Post 4 reels/month on Instagram (Canva mockups → WhatsApp design-approval screenshots → pilot delivery photos). Run 10 DMs/day to club/fest Instagram handles found via #<college>fest, #<college>club. Hold the ₹3,500 boost until AFTER the first organic order closes: then put the full ₹3,500 into ONE boost on the single reel that already produced a WhatsApp reply, CTA button = 'Send WhatsApp message', audience = 18-24 year olds within 10km of campus, interest targets = college fests + streetwear. Cap it at 7 days; count a conversion only as a WhatsApp thread that reaches a mockup request — if 0 mockup requests in 7 days, stop and return to organic DMs.

first_10_customers: Pre-week-1 (before any cold outreach): close 1 warm pilot — a batchmate-run club or your own class fest, 25-unit Club Tee at ₹349/unit with 1 free design revision, 7-day delivery guarantee in writing, 50% advance via Razorpay link. Deliver flawlessly, collect 1 delivery photo + a 2-line WhatsApp testimonial. This is your only proof asset for cold outreach.

Week 1: List 30 clubs/fests at your own college and 2 neighbouring colleges in a Google Sheet (name, head, WhatsApp, Instagram, last event date, expected units). Message 10/day starting with juniors and batchmates who run clubs.

Week 1-2: Send the 3-line cold message + a Canva mockup of THEIR club logo on a tee to 10 club heads/day on WhatsApp, attaching the pilot delivery photo as proof. Log every reply in the Sheet. Follow up day 3 and day 7 with 'want me to send a free digital mockup of your exact design?'

Week 2-3: Convert customer #2 with a locked-in pilot: 50-unit Fest Tee order, 7-day delivery guarantee written on WhatsApp, 50% advance via Razorpay. Ask for a 2-line WhatsApp testimonial + referral to one other club head.

Week 3-4: Ask every existing contact (batchmates, hostel WhatsApp groups, seniors in fest committees) for 1 warm intro to a club head. Post 1 Instagram reel of the delivered order with the college tag. Target 3 intros/week.

Week 4-6: Chase orders 3-5 via referrals from customers #1 and #2 (offer 1 free hoodie on their next order as a referral reward — reduces revenue, not spend). Run the ₹3,500 reel boost only after order #2 closes. Lock Day-30 target of 1 paying customer (50-unit Fest Tee, 50% advance via Razorpay) plus a pipeline of 3 warm conversations for Day-60.
growth.cold_message: Hi [Name], I saw [Club/Fest] is coming up on [date] — do you already have T-shirts sorted for your team/volunteers? I print 50+ unit club and fest orders (180 GSM, 2-colour design) with a 7-day delivery guarantee and 50% advance, and I'll send you a free mockup of your own logo on the tee today if you share the design. Want me to send it over?

objections.objection: Local print shop near college quoted me cheaper / I can get it done for less.
objections.response: Ask what their lead time and revision policy are — most college-area shops quote 10-14 days with no digital preview, and one missed date kills your merch plan. My quote is ₹329/unit for 50+ with a 7-day delivery guarantee written on WhatsApp, 1 free design revision, and a digital mockup approved before printing. If they beat that with a written date, I'll match it — otherwise you're betting your event on a shop that can't commit.

objections.objection: I need to check with my committee / budget isn't approved yet.
objections.response: Totally fair — I can hold your slot for 48 hours with no payment. Send me your logo and event name and I'll send a free mockup within 2 hours so your committee sees exactly what they're approving. Once approved, it's just a Razorpay link for 50% advance and we start printing — you only pay the balance on delivery.

critic.verdict: The plan is a faithful, well-scoped execution of the stated idea: bulk custom-printed tees and hoodies for college clubs and fests in India, bootstrapped by a student founder. Tools, channels, pricing and payment flow all fit the HARD RULES (campus-first, UPI/Razorpay, near-zero burn, 15 hrs/week). The main viability question is whether a no-track-record founder can reliably close 1-2 bulk orders per month at these price points within the first 60 days.
critic.biggest_risk: The founder has no delivery track record and no samples in hand, so club heads and fest treasurers — who are accountable for their event's merch — may simply not trust an unknown student with a 50% advance and a hard event deadline, stalling the pipeline past the 6-week window.
